channel.title: Luvia Blog
channel.description: Quiet, evidence-led writing on rituals, mood and kindness.

item.title: Meditation for Focus: What Ten Minutes a Day Does to Attention
item.description: Does meditation improve attention? What the studies actually show, how big the effect is, and a plain ten-minute focus protocol with a silent timer.

item.title: WOOP for Focus: A Plan for the Moment You Reach for Your Phone
item.description: Use WOOP on one focus wish: ninety quiet minutes each morning for two weeks. The obstacle is the itch to check, and the plan fires the moment it arrives.

item.title: Meditation when focusing on the breath makes it worse
item.description: If watching your breath makes you more anxious, not less, you are not doing it wrong. Here are six other anchors and how to choose one.

item.title: Counting meditation: the technique you cannot get wrong
item.description: Count to ten, lose your place, start again. Three ways to meditate by counting, where it comes from, what the research says, and why losing count is the point.

item.title: WOOP Wish Examples: How to Pick a Goal That Sticks
item.description: Most WOOPs fail at the first word. Learn Oettingen's three tests for a wish, why 'be happier' stalls, and see one wish reshaped until it sticks.

item.title: Name It to Tame It: Why Labelling a Mood Calms It
item.description: Putting a feeling into words quietly turns it down. What affect labelling research found, why precise words beat a score, and how to do a two-word check-in.

item.title: Writing a Letter to Your Future Self (and Why It Works)
item.description: What the research on future self-continuity says about writing to yourself, how to pick the date, what to put in it, and why sealing the letter matters.

item.title: WOOP Obstacle Examples: Finding the Honest One Inside You
item.description: WOOP only works with an inner obstacle: a habit, feeling or belief, not time, money or other people. Why that rule exists, the common dodges, and one example.

item.title: How to Meditate for the First Time: A Five-Minute Version
item.description: A plain first meditation in five steps: sit, set a timer, pick one anchor, expect to wander, come back. What a first session feels like and how often to do it.

item.title: The WOOP Plan: Writing an If-Then That Fires on Its Own
item.description: The last step of WOOP is one if-then sentence. Here is how to write one that fires by itself, what the research says, and why trying harder is not a plan.

item.title: Three Good Things: What the Gratitude Research Really Shows
item.description: The three good things exercise has twenty years of trials behind it. The effect is real and modest. What the studies found, and how to do it without forcing it.

item.title: Why Being Kind to a Stranger Helps You Too
item.description: What the research says about acts of kindness and wellbeing, the honest finding about anonymous kindness and loneliness, and how a reply changes it.

item.title: WOOP: the manifestation method with science behind it
item.description: Wishing is where every good change starts. WOOP keeps the wishing and adds the step that makes it move: naming the obstacle.

item.title: Is Luvia safe? A plain answer from the people who make it
item.description: What never leaves your device, what anonymity structurally prevents, and how moderation works.

item.title: The best private mood tracker apps for iPhone (2026)
item.description: Five trackers that respect your privacy, ranked by where the data lives and how the business makes money.

item.title: Luvia vs Daylio vs Bearable: which fits you?
item.description: Three good apps that want different things for you: speed, health data, or calm.

item.title: The best meditation and manifestation apps for 2026
item.description: Guided meditation, free libraries, quiet timers, and the one manifestation method with evidence.
